title: Stimulus, receptor and effector
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:59Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point 'Homeostasis' covers the same stimulus, receptor, control centre and effector chain but is framed around homeostasis at a senior Biology depth, with the hypothalamus and brainstem, so it is broader and deeper than this Year 9 point on stimulus, receptor and effector.

draft.title: Stimulus, receptor and effector
card: a change inside or outside the body that the body can detect, such as a loud noise or a drop in body temperature.
a cell or organ that detects a stimulus. The eyes, ears and skin hold receptors.
a part, such as the brain, that takes in the information from receptors and decides how to respond.
a muscle or gland that carries out the response. A muscle moves a body part, and a gland releases a substance.
draft.remember: The body detects a change, decides what to do, then acts on it.

a.q: Ravi hears a car horn and jumps back onto the footpath. Which part of this is the stimulus?
opts: The sound of the car horn
The leg muscles moving him back
a.why: The stimulus is the change that is detected, which is the sound. The ears are the receptors, the brain is the control centre, and the leg muscles are the effectors. The ears are tempting but they detect the stimulus and are not the stimulus.
a.clue: The stimulus is the change itself, not the part that detects it.

b.q: Lena smells hot chips and her mouth begins to water. Which is the effector?
b.why: The effector carries out the response, and here the response is saliva being released by the glands. The nose is the receptor that detects the smell. The brain decides, but it does not produce the response itself.
b.clue: Which part actually produces the response?

a.best: The sound of the car horn
